kinds.a: urine dipstick · urinalysis strips · UTI test
kinds.d: Paper strips with reagent pads dipped in urine to show infection markers or other values by colour change.

kinds.a: home HIV test · HIV home test kit
kinds.d: Over-the-counter rapid test that detects HIV antibodies from an oral swab or a drop of fingerstick blood.

kinds.a: faecal immunochemical test · FIT · home bowel cancer test · stool test
kinds.d: Home stool-sample kit that checks for hidden blood, a possible sign of bowel cancer, and is posted to a laboratory.

kinds.a: home cholesterol test · lipid test kit · cholesterol meter
kinds.d: Fingerstick test or small meter that measures blood cholesterol at home.

kinds.a: breathalyzer · personal breathalyser · alcohol tester · alcohol meter
kinds.d: Handheld device that estimates blood alcohol from a breath sample, for checking you are fit to drive.

kinds.a: software as a medical device · SaMD · digital therapeutic
kinds.d: Software that itself diagnoses or treats, or is cleared as a medical device; an app that only shows readings from a separate device is not this.

notes: Shelf rebuilt to 7 kinds (was 2: k58 Infection test kit, k62 Medical app). New kinds: Urine test strips, HIV self-test, Bowel screening test, Cholesterol test, Breathalyser, each sourced to a page retrieved this session. Infection test kit: corrected Flowflex maker to ACON Laboratories (per aconlabs.com) and added iHealth; kept the old 2SAN and FaStep entries. Breathalyser models come from the AlcoSense Wikipedia article, a Parkers best-buy review (AlcoSense Pro, Lite 2 and Excel were its picks), the Dräger product finder and BACtrack's site. BACtrack Mobile and S80 were seen only in search-result titles, not on a fetched page. Bowel screening test has no models: FIT kits are mostly handed out by health services, and I could not retrieve a source for Cologuard (the Wikipedia hit was a golf tournament). It is named only as a type. Medical app: added SleepioRx (AASM page on its FDA clearance). Left out Clue Birth Control because Natural Cycles' site says it is the only FDA-cleared birth-control app, which conflicts. HbA1c kits (A1CNow+) belong to the Diabetes care shelf, so they are not here. No food-intolerance or other unproven-claim tests were added. No traditions apply to this shelf. BACtrack and OraSure have no founding year because no retrieved page gave one.
